$comment: Coverage floors enforced by scripts/coverage-gate.mjs (.github/workflows/coverage-gate.yml). 'measured' is the Jest reading on main 565da3d1 (CI, Node 22: the coverage-gate.yml and auto-qa.yml runs of 2026-10-19 agree; backend: npm run backend:test:coverage, frontend: npm run frontend:test:coverage, both with --coverageReporters=json-summary), except backend-modules, measured on main 81e28a43 with backend/jest.config.js widened to modules, utils and shared (local run, PostgreSQL 16; the backend area's figures from that run equal the CI coverage-gate run of the same commit). 'floor' sits about 3 points below measured so ordinary churn passes but a real drop fails. Floors only go up: .github/workflows/auto-qa.yml proposes raises via a tracking issue (rules in .github/auto-qa-tuning.json). Raising a floor makes the check catch more, so it is the 'Adding or widening a check' case in AGENTS.md's owner's standing decisions: an agent may raise one without asking. Lowering a floor, or exempting anything from it, needs the owner. Scope is whatever each Jest config's collectCoverageFrom selects, narrowed by an area's 'include' folders when it has one: the backend run covers models, middleware, services, modules, utils and shared; the backend area counts models, middleware and services, and backend-modules counts modules, utils and shared, so both read the one backend summary. Frontend covers frontend/**/*.{ts,tsx}. Frontend has known failing suites on main (MermaidDiagram, MarkdownRenderer.publicLinks, roleLabels, Layout, markdownTaskList); Jest still writes coverage for the rest, so the number is slightly understated.
